evidence.note: Directly reduces backward error propagation by decoupling client-server training and removing gradient exchange.
Uses local error routing to avoid transported weights/random feedback; shared architecture and error-signal handling are central.
Explicitly shares one DReLU across many neurons/layers to cut costly nonlinearity computation in shared channels.
Federated learning compression with error feedback reduces communication overhead, but not specifically shared neural architectures.
Predictive coding uses highway error propagation to manage error flow in very deep networks; still propagates errors rather than avoiding them.
Modular experts isolate pathways and signals, but focus is robustness/efficiency rather than avoiding error-signal propagation.
Neuron merging/compression via activation mapping and clustering; no clear error-signal propagation reduction.
Low-rank modular neuronal communication and information sharing, but not about error propagation or data exchange.
Approximate convolution reduces MACs for inference, unrelated to error signal propagation or shared architectures.
Operator learning with kernel corrections; no relevant shared-architecture error exchange mechanism.
